column1: # tools/ci-expected.tsv -- the allow-list `tools/ci-census.py` checks a build against.
# One row per allowed skip. Tab separated:
# `bench_total` is the number of cases the suite prints WHEN EVERYTHING IT NEEDS
# IS PRESENT -- measured on the bench machine 2026-08-25, not read off the
# source. `covers` is how many cases that one skip LINE stands for, and it is
# the field that matters: on a stock runner `tools/test-hazlint.sh` prints eight
# skip lines standing for twenty-five cases, and a census that counted lines
# A suite with nothing to skip gets one row with `-` and 0.
# A suite CI does not run at all is marked `*bench-only*`, and its whole total
# counts as not run. It is listed rather than omitted because a suite nobody
# lists is a suite nobody misses.

column5: needs a filesystem that can make symlinks; MSYS/Git Bash cannot, and until 2026-08-25 that killed the whole suite under errexit on the machine the push happens from. CI runs on Linux, so this skip should NOT appear
needs binutils-mips-linux-gnu; CI installs it, so this skip should NOT appear

needs gcc-mips-linux-gnu -- and CI deliberately does NOT install it, because with the cross compiler present the suite BUILDS and then hazlint refuses to report without its stage2.bin population control, which is correct behaviour; re-measured 2026-08-25 (second sitting) with $FWRE_WORK empty it is 56 ok / 50 FAIL

its K4 population control is $FWRE_WORK/stage2.bin -- 56 KiB of this unit's own vendor bootloader, which is someone else's property and identifies one physical device. On a runner the suite does not skip, it FAILS 14 cases, because hazlint exits 2 rather than report without that control
